newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish conservatives oppose govt EMU decision.
newsitem.headline: Swedish conservatives oppose govt EMU decision.

text.p: Sweden's main opposition party, the conservative Moderate Party, on Tuesday criticised the ruling Social Democrats decision to remain outside Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) at its planned start in 1999.
"The Social Democratic party leadership's no to the common euro currency shows lack of leadership and political responsibility," Lars Tobisson, deputy leader of the Moderates, said in a statement.
"This will lead to higher interest rates and other economic hardships in Sweden but also to a reduced Swedish influence in Europe."

The ruling Social Democratic party sought to keep the door open for EMU membership some time in the future by leaving it up to the people to decide through a normal election, a snap election or a referendum.
